history.summary: CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name - this temple is in KARNATAKA (town Aihole), not the value shown in the CSV. The best-known temple at Aihole, an early Chalukyan structural temple of the late 7th century built on a rare apsidal (gajaprishta, 'elephant's back') plan echoing Buddhist chaitya halls - a hallmark of Aihole's experimental architecture. Raised on a high moulded adhisthana, with a pillared corridor wrapping the shrine, mukhamandapa and sabhamandapa for circumambulation; incomplete tower over the sanctuary. The name 'Durga' comes from a nearby fort/fortified enclosure (the building reportedly served as a military outpost, possibly Maratha-period), not from the goddess - the original deity is unknown, with Surya or Vishnu proposed. Carved panels depict Durga as Mahishasuramardini, Vishnu avatars (Varaha, Narasimha), Shiva with Nandi, Harihara and river goddesses. ASI-protected monument; no active pooja or prasadam.

name: Durga Temple
town_description: Aihole in Bagalkot district, Karnataka, was an early Chalukya capital and is called the 'cradle of Indian temple architecture' for its 100+ experimental 6th-12th century temples. Together with Badami and Pattadakal it forms the Chalukyan architectural triangle; the Durga temple complex sits by the Malaprabha river with an ASI archaeological museum nearby.
